title: Anomalous Behavior Recognition and User Guidance

slides.title: Anomalous Behavior Recognition and User Guidance
points: Awareness training should help users recognize suspicious behavior and apply secure practices in everyday work, especially around social engineering, passwords, removable media, and remote environments.

slides.title: Risky Behavior

blocks.title: Anomalous Behavior Recognition and User Guidance comparison
Anomalous Behavior Recognition and User Guidance exam shortcuts
items: User knowingly bypasses security for convenience → RISKY
Example: Employee disables endpoint protection to install software.
Activity does not fit the user's normal pattern → UNEXPECTED
Unexpected behavior is anomalous, even if the cause is not yet known.
Example: User downloads thousands of files at 3 AM.
Mistake causes exposure with no malicious intent → UNINTENTIONAL
The security impact came from human error.
Example: Employee emails a confidential file to the wrong recipient.
Unknown USB drive or cable → DO NOT TRUST IT
Removable media can introduce malware or hardware-based attacks.
Example: Turn found media over to security rather than plugging it in.
Attacker manipulates a person instead of exploiting software → SOCIAL ENGINEERING
The human is the attack surface.
Example: Caller impersonates IT and asks for an MFA code.
Working from home or travel location → REMOTE-WORK SECURITY
Users still need secure networks, device protection, and privacy.
Example: Use approved VPN and avoid exposing sensitive screens in public.
blocks.example: First identify the human-security problem: phishing, suspicious behavior, user guidance, or awareness-program measurement.

questions.q: An employee disables endpoint protection because it interferes with software installation. What type of behavior is this?
questions.explanation: The employee knowingly increases exposure by bypassing a security control.

questions.q: A user who normally downloads a few files suddenly downloads thousands at 3 AM. What type of behavior is this?
questions.explanation: The activity deviates from the user's normal behavior and is therefore unexpected/anomalous.

questions.q: An employee accidentally emails a confidential file to the wrong recipient. What type of behavior is this?
questions.explanation: The security impact was caused by accidental human error.

questions.q: A caller impersonates the IT department and asks an employee for an MFA code. What awareness topic applies?
questions.explanation: The attacker is manipulating the user rather than directly exploiting software.

questions.q: An employee finds an unknown USB drive in the parking lot. What should awareness training recommend?
choices: Do not plug it in; turn it over to security
Test it on a personal laptop
Plug it in with antivirus disabled
questions.explanation: Unknown removable media should not be trusted or connected to organizational devices.

questions.q: An employee is working in a coffee shop with sensitive data visible on screen. Which awareness area is most relevant?
choices: Hybrid/remote work security and situational awareness
questions.explanation: Remote-work security includes protecting devices, networks, and privacy in public environments.

questions.q: A user posts internal deployment schedules and system details on social media. Which awareness concept is most relevant?
questions.explanation: OPSEC focuses on avoiding unnecessary disclosure of sensitive operational information.
